faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Otolaryngology and Rhinoplasty
faq.question1: When should I see an otolaryngologist?
faq.answer1:
It is recommended to seek care when you experience:

Persistent nasal obstruction
Snoring or sleep apnea
Frequent sinusitis
Throat pain or recurrent infections
Voice changes
Dizziness or hearing loss
Swelling or lumps in the neck
faq.question2: What is an otolaryngology consultation like?
faq.answer2:
The consultation begins with a detailed clinical interview, evaluating:

Current symptoms
Medical and surgical history
Allergies
Habits (smoking, medication use, etc.)
History of recurrent infections or respiratory problems

Afterwards, a specialized physical examination of the ears, nose, and throat is performed.

Depending on the case, additional studies may be ordered such as:

Imaging studies (X-rays or CT scans)
Allergy tests
Hearing tests
Cultures or specific analyses
faq.question3: How is a rhinoplasty evaluation conducted?

The evaluation includes:

Comprehensive facial analysis (proportions, symmetry, and facial harmony)
Functional assessment of nasal breathing
Study of the septum and internal structures
Clinical photographs
Detailed explanation of realistic expectations and possible results
faq.question4: When will I see the results?

The change is visible as soon as the splint is removed (approximately 7–10 days).

However:

Swelling progressively decreases during the first 3 months.

Patience is key, as the nose is a structure that heals and reduces swelling gradually

ear.title_h1: Balance Disorders: Vertigo and Dizziness - Why Do They Occur and When to See a Specialist?
ear.intro_text: Feeling like everything is spinning around you or losing stability is one of the most common reasons for consultation with Dr. Lumbán. Understanding how the balance system works helps identify symptoms and seek medical attention.
ear.what_is_vertigo_text: Vertigo is a balance disorder characterized by a false sensation of movement, usually described as if everything is spinning around you or as if you are spinning.
ear.vertigo_symptoms_title: During episodes, the following may occur:
ear.vertigo_cause: Vertigo is usually caused by an alteration of the vestibular system, located in the inner ear, which controls balance.
ear.vertigo_types_text: For diagnosis, we classify vertigo into two main groups:
ear.vertigo_peripheral: Peripheral Vertigo: This is the most common type. It is caused by an alteration in the labyrinth or the vestibular nerve. It often includes auditory symptoms such as ringing or pressure in the ear.
ear.vertigo_central: Central Vertigo: This originates from alterations in the brain or brainstem. Instability is usually very pronounced and may include double vision.
ear.what_is_dizziness_text: Dizziness is a sensation of instability or 'empty head.' It may include impending fainting, cold sweating, paleness, nausea, and general discomfort.
ear.dizziness_note: Unlike vertigo, dizziness does not always involve a spinning sensation and may be related to circulatory, neurological, or metabolic problems.
ear.balance_system_title: How Does Our Balance Work? The Role of the Inner Ear
ear.balance_system_text: Balance does not depend on a single organ but on several systems coordinated by the brain.
ear.balance_systems_list:
Vestibular system (inner ear)
Visual system
Musculoskeletal and proprioceptive system
ear.brain_balance: The brain combines information from these systems to maintain posture and body orientation.
ear.inner_ear_title: The Inner Ear and the Vestibular System
ear.inner_ear_text: Inside the inner ear there is a structure called the labyrinth, made up of bone and soft tissues filled with fluid. This system detects head movements and body position.
ear.semicircular_canals_text: They are three tubes filled with fluid that detect head rotations. Inside them, a gelatinous structure called the cupula acts like a 'ship's sail' that moves with the fluid, and sensory cells with small extensions called stereocilia.
ear.head_movement4: A nerve signal is generated to the brain indicating the direction of movement.
ear.otolithic_text: These structures inform the brain and detect gravity. Thanks to them, the brain knows whether you are sitting, lying down, or moving sideways.
ear.balance_failure: If any of these signals fail, a balance disorder appears.
ear.balance_disorder_symptoms_text: In addition to the spinning sensation, balance disorders may manifest as:
ear.symptom1: Difficulty walking in a straight line or staggering.
ear.symptom3: Feeling of floating or impending fall.
ear.causes_title: Frequent Causes of Vertigo and Dizziness
ear.causes_text: Balance problems can originate from multiple factors:
ear.common_diseases_title: Most Common Diseases Related to Vertigo
ear.bppv_text: Occurs when small calcium crystals (otoliths) detach and float in the ear canals, causing brief but intense vertigo when moving the head.
ear.labyrinthitis_text: Inflammation or infection of the inner ear, usually associated with viral respiratory infections. It can cause:
ear.meniere_text: It is characterized by recurrent episodes of:
ear.meniere_note: It is related to alterations of the fluid within the labyrinth.
ear.fistula_text: A fluid leak in the inner ear, common after trauma or sudden pressure changes.
ear.warning_signs_title: Warning Signs: When to See an Otolaryngologist?
ear.warning_signs_text: If dizziness or vertigo is accompanied by the following symptoms:
ear.warning1: Severe headache or sudden neck pain.
ear.warning4: Weakness or numbness in arms or legs.
ear.warning_note: These symptoms may indicate a serious neurological cause
ear.self_assessment_title: Self-Assessment: Should You Consult Dr. Lumbán?
ear.self_assessment_text: If you answered 'yes' to any of these questions, it is recommended to have a professional evaluation:
ear.question1: Do you feel like the room is spinning?
ear.question2: Do you lose balance and fall frequently?
ear.question3: Do you feel like you are going to faint when standing up?
ear.question4: Does your vision become blurry during episodes?
ear.self_assessment_note: Vertigo and dizziness should not be considered normal symptoms. Although many causes are benign, some may indicate diseases that require specialized diagnosis.
ear.conclusion: An appropriate otolaryngological evaluation allows identifying the origin of the problem and offering effective treatments that significantly improve quality of life.
ear.cta_text: Would you like to schedule an evaluation to assess your symptoms in a personalized way?
ear.cta_phone: Write to us or call us at (664) 684 2364 | (664) 638 8135
ear.balance_description1: Our balance is a complex interaction that requires strong communication between our ears, eyes, and the sense of touch based on the perception of our feet, muscles, and joints. To maintain our center of gravity, our central nervous system must receive these three signals and then correctly transmit them to the brain.
ear.balance_description2: When signals from our senses do not reach the cerebellum, or reach it with the wrong message, we experience this lack of communication as a loss of balance, dizziness.
ear.balance_description3: A balance disorder can sometimes be a symptom of other medical conditions. Proper medical care, including a complete medical history and evaluation of the balance system, is important to identify the cause and provide appropriate treatment options.
ear.vertigo_description: It is the perception of spinning, movement, or rotation of either oneself or the surrounding environment. It is usually episodic rather than constant.
ear.imbalance_description: It is a sensation of instability or loss of balance, whether at rest or when walking, or both. It is often described as a feeling of 'being on a boat.' These symptoms may or may not be accompanied by a feeling of clogged ears, hearing loss, or ringing in the ears.
ear.cause_fluid_buildup: Fluid buildup in the inner ear. Ménière's disease
ear.evaluation_text: If you have balance problems or dizziness, we will complete a comprehensive evaluation. Our balance laboratory can perform a series of tests to help diagnose and treat your problem.
ear.vestibular_rehab_description: "Vestibular rehabilitation" is a series of exercises for balance recovery. They can be performed at home or by an audiologist, and each rehabilitation program is specifically designed to correct the patient's balance disorders.
ear.canal_repositioning_description: Many cases of vertigo can be resolved with a simple positioning procedure in the office. Canal repositioning maneuvers are treatments that guide the patient through a series of head and body positions designed to move loosened otoconia (crystals) back into the balance organ.
ear.lifestyle_description: Caffeine, salt, alcohol, nicotine, and dehydration can all have a considerable impact on the sense of balance. Dr. Lumbán will provide you with medications and recommendations about diet and daily habits so that your balance problems can continue to be controlled at home.

hearing-loss.title_h1: Hearing Loss: Everything You Need to Know About Your Ears with an Otolaryngologist
hearing-loss.intro_text: Hearing loss is considered disabling when it exceeds 35 decibels (dB) in the ear with better hearing ability. This condition can range from mild to profound, affecting one or both ears, making it difficult to understand conversations or detect loud sounds.
hearing-loss.gradual_text: A key issue with hearing loss is that it is usually gradual. Because it develops slowly over years, the patient often only becomes aware of the problem when it has already advanced significantly.
hearing-loss.classification_title: Classification and Types of Hearing Loss
hearing-loss.classification_text: Hearing loss, also known as hearing impairment, is classified according to the area of the auditory system that is affected:
hearing-loss.conductive_text: This occurs when there is an obstacle preventing sound from reaching the sensory structures of the inner ear. The problem may be located in the external ear canal, the eardrum, or the middle ear.
hearing-loss.conductive_note: It makes sounds seem muffled. This type of hearing loss can often be corrected through medical or surgical intervention.
hearing-loss.conductive_cause1: fluid in the middle ear due to colds or allergies
hearing-loss.conductive_cause3: Eustachian tube dysfunction (a narrow tube connecting the middle ear to the throat)
hearing-loss.sensorineural_text: This is the most common type of permanent hearing loss. It occurs when sound reaches the inner ear but cannot be translated into nerve impulses, or the nerve impulses are not carried to the brain. It is generally not repairable through medical or surgical intervention.
hearing-loss.sensorineural_causes_title: Some possible causes of this type of hearing loss include:
hearing-loss.mixed_text: This is a combination of the two previous types. It can be caused by severe head trauma, chronic infection, or a genetic disorder.
hearing-loss.mixed_example: An example of mixed hearing loss would be if a person who normally has sensorineural hearing loss also developed an ear infection.
hearing-loss.specific_causes_title: Specific Causes and Common Hearing Loss Pathologies
hearing-loss.specific_causes_text: In addition to the general types, there are specific conditions that Dr. Lumbán frequently evaluates:
hearing-loss.cerumen_text: Sometimes wax accumulates in the ear canal and, in some cases, can completely block it. This often happens with hearing aid use, as the mold or casing tends to compress cerumen in the ear canal, which can lead to the formation of plugs that substantially reduce hearing.
hearing-loss.noise_text: Exposure to extreme noise (such as a firearm or nearby explosion) can cause sudden hearing loss, known as acoustic trauma. Hearing loss caused by acoustic trauma usually disappears within a day (unless the shockwave has also injured the eardrum or middle ear).
hearing-loss.noise_note: However, it is long-term exposure to noise that causes most noise-induced hearing loss.
hearing-loss.infections_title: Ear Infections (especially in children and young adults)
hearing-loss.infections_text: Otitis and Cholesteatoma: Infections can be acute (from bacteria from the pharynx) or chronic (from eardrum perforation). Chronic otitis can lead to cholesteatoma, a mass of cells with benign tumor-like behavior that requires specialized attention.
hearing-loss.otosclerosis_text: It is a middle ear disease where bone growth around the stapes prevents the ossicles from vibrating properly, making sound transmission difficult.
hearing-loss.warning_signs_title: How Do I Know If I'm Losing My Hearing? (Warning Signs)
hearing-loss.warning_signs_text: If you or a family member present the following signs, it's time to schedule a consultation with Dr. Lumbán:
hearing-loss.warning1: Difficulty understanding specific words during a conversation
hearing-loss.warning2: Frequently asking for words to be repeated
hearing-loss.warning4: Avoiding social situations due to difficulty hearing others
hearing-loss.warning5: Problems following conversation in groups or in the presence of background noise
hearing-loss.warning6: Noises in the ear such as ringing, roaring, whistling, buzzing, etc.
hearing-loss.degrees_text: To measure severity, specialists use the decibel scale (dB HL)
hearing-loss.aging_text: Older people often experience a progressive decrease in hearing called presbycusis. Statistics show a notable increase over the years:
hearing-loss.aging_stat1: 45 to 54 years: 5% have disabling hearing loss.
hearing-loss.aging_stat2: 55 to 64 years: The rate increases to 10%.
hearing-loss.aging_stat4: 75 years or older: Up to 55% of the population is affected.
hearing-loss.prevention_title: Prevention: How to Care for Your Ears?
hearing-loss.prevention_text: Limiting exposure to loud noises is the best prevention strategy. It is essential to control both the duration and intensity of sound.
hearing-loss.protection_text: If you regularly find yourself in noisy environments, strict protective measures will be necessary:
hearing-loss.protection2: Protective earmuffs: Especially those filled with glycerin that completely cover the ear.
hearing-loss.protection3: Safety rule: Any noise above 85 decibels (dB) can cause damage if exposure is prolonged.
hearing-loss.cta_appointment_text: If you or a family member begin to have difficulty understanding conversations or hearing clearly, we invite you to schedule your otolaryngology consultation with Dr. Jaime Lumbán. Our goal is to find a personalized solution to the hearing problem and prevent future complications.
hearing-loss.about_subtitle: To hear what you've lost, have your hearing thoroughly evaluated.
hearing-loss.stat_text: At any given time, about 30 million Americans are affected by hearing loss. Hearing loss disproportionately affects adults. And while it is more common among older adults, hearing loss is also a fact of life for adults in their 40s and 50s, not just for those over 65.
hearing-loss.gradual_description: A key issue with hearing loss is that it is usually gradual. While it can be sudden, hearing loss generally develops slowly over several years. The result is that most people with hearing loss are not aware of the extent of their problem.
hearing-loss.severity_text: It is also important to remember that hearing loss does not mean a total inability to hear. Hearing loss can be mild, moderate, severe, or total.
hearing-loss.sign1: Does not understand some words during conversation
hearing-loss.sign2: Frequently asks for words to be repeated
hearing-loss.sign3: Friends and family express concern about hearing
hearing-loss.sign5: Avoids social situations due to difficulty hearing others
hearing-loss.sign6: Problems following conversation in groups or in the presence of background noise
hearing-loss.sign7: Noises in the ear such as ringing, roaring, whistling, buzzing, etc.
hearing-loss.causes_title: Causes of Hearing Loss in Adults
hearing-loss.causes_text: Hearing loss in adults is most commonly the result of damage to the inner ear structure or the auditory nerve. It can be caused by aging, diseases, certain medications, injuries, infections, and noise exposure. While this type of hearing loss is not usually reversible, you can do something about it. The first thing to do is to have your hearing studied and determine the nature and extent of your hearing loss.

septoplasty.title_h1: Septoplasty: Nasal Septum Correction to Improve Breathing
septoplasty.intro_text: Nasal septum correction, known as septoplasty, is one of the most common procedures in otolaryngology. The nasal septum is the wall of bone and cartilage that divides the two nasal passages; when deviated, whether by birth or due to trauma, it can obstruct the passage of air.
septoplasty.common_text: Having a deviated septum is common, but if it is too deviated, it can obstruct airflow. This makes breathing difficult through one or both sides of the nose.
septoplasty.anatomy_title: Anatomy of Your Nose: How Does It Work?
septoplasty.anatomy_text: The nasal septum performs fundamental functions: it provides structural support to the nose and directs airflow in a balanced manner. The septum is made of thin bone in the back and cartilage in the front.
septoplasty.anatomy_note: A crooked septum can make breathing difficult. It can also cause snoring and sleep apnea.
septoplasty.symptom1: Persistent difficulty breathing through the nose.
septoplasty.symptom3: Sensation of nasal dryness or irritation.
septoplasty.surgery_title: Surgery: What Does a Septoplasty Involve?
septoplasty.surgery_text: Septoplasty aims to correct or reconstruct the deviated septum. Depending on the patient's needs, it can be performed alone or combined with rhinoplasty (aesthetic), turbinate surgery, or nasal valve surgery.
septoplasty.surgery_detail: During septoplasty, the septum is repositioned back to the center of the nose. To do this, Dr. Lumbán first reshapes, removes, or reinserts parts of the cartilage and bone in the correct position to open the airways.
septoplasty.incision_desc: It is achieved through a small incision inside the nostril, so it leaves no visible scars.
septoplasty.outpatient_desc: It is a procedure that usually takes less than an hour and does not require hospitalization.
septoplasty.recovery_desc: The vast majority of patients report minimal pain and can return to desk work within 3 to 5 days.
septoplasty.advanced_technique_text: Dr. Lumbán does not use nasal packing that blocks the passage of air after surgery. This allows the patient to leave the hospital breathing without obstruction, from the very first moment.
septoplasty.benefit1: Improved Breathing: Restores airflow, improving not only breathing but also sleep quality.
septoplasty.benefit2: Treatment for Apnea: Used as an auxiliary treatment in patients with sleep apnea, improving rest quality.
septoplasty.benefit3: Sports Performance: Beneficial for athletes who need adequate airflow during physical activity.
septoplasty.benefit4: Improved Sleep: Patients who previously breathed through their mouth while sleeping now enjoy natural nasal breathing.
septoplasty.differences_title: Main Differences Between Septoplasty and Rhinoplasty
septoplasty.differences_text: It is essential to distinguish between septoplasty and rhinoplasty, as both are surgical interventions on the nose but with different objectives.
septoplasty.differences_note: Septoplasty focuses on the functioning of the nasal septum, while rhinoplasty deals with the aesthetics of the nose.
septoplasty.differences_combined: Sometimes, both procedures can be combined to address both functional and aesthetic problems.
septoplasty.recovery_evolution_title: Evolution and Final Results of Septoplasty: What to Expect?
septoplasty.recovery_day1: First days: Mild swelling and congestion are normal, which decrease significantly by the end of the first week.
septoplasty.recovery_day10: At 10 days: Most patients resume their daily activities with basic precautions.
septoplasty.recovery_complete: Complete recovery: Tissue usually feels fully restored between 4 and 6 weeks.
septoplasty.recovery_note: Although respiratory improvement is evident soon, total septum stability and definitive tissue changes can take 3 to 6 months, or even up to a year to fully consolidate.

sinusitis.hero_subtitle: Specialized treatment for acute and chronic sinusitis
sinusitis.title_h1: Acute and Chronic Sinusitis: What is the Best Specialized Treatment?
sinusitis.intro_text: Sinusitis refers to inflammation within the nose, specifically the paranasal sinus cavities. It is classified as acute (short-term symptoms lasting 1-12 weeks) and chronic sinusitis (longer-lasting symptoms, 12 weeks or more).
sinusitis.intro_text2: This common condition prevents proper mucus drainage, causing nasal congestion, difficulty breathing, and tenderness or swelling around the eyes.
sinusitis.cause1: Infections: Frequent colds or other viral or bacterial infections affecting the sinuses.
sinusitis.cause2: Anatomical problems: Internal obstructions such as deviated nasal septum, nasal polyps, or tumors.
sinusitis.symptom1: Nasal congestion: Difficulty breathing due to inflammation and mucus buildup.
sinusitis.symptom2: Purulent discharge: Thick yellow or green mucus.
sinusitis.symptom3: Nasal drip: Constant flow of discolored mucus.
sinusitis.symptom4: Post-nasal drip: Sensation of mucus and discomfort in the back of the throat.
sinusitis.symptom5: Pain and pressure: Tenderness and swelling in eyes, cheeks, forehead, and throat.
sinusitis.diagnosis_text: Dr. Lumbán will conduct a comprehensive evaluation, including a detailed medical history, ENT examination (Complete evaluation of ears, nose, throat, larynx, and neck). This procedure is easily performed in the office with minimal discomfort, providing an accurate diagnosis, especially in cases of sinusitis.
sinusitis.treatment_text: Acute sinusitis is usually treated with antibiotics, anti-inflammatories, nasal decongestants, and corticosteroids (oral or injectable). If symptoms persist, advanced intervention may be required:
sinusitis.balloon_text: A minimally invasive procedure that helps eliminate trapped mucus by dilating the nasal passages.
sinusitis.cens_text: Indicated for patients with refractory inflammation (unresponsive to medical treatment), significant nasal obstruction, or anatomical abnormalities.
sinusitis.cens_note: This surgery prioritizes preservation of sinus function while restoring proper drainage. It is typically performed under general anesthesia on an outpatient basis (no hospitalization required).
sinusitis.cta_final: Breathe freely again. If conventional treatments haven't worked, it's time for a specialized evaluation. Dr. Lumbán offers minimally invasive solutions to help you return to your routine without discomfort. Schedule your evaluation today
sinusitis.stat_text: Sinusitis is one of the most common medical conditions requiring treatment annually in the United States. Generally speaking, sinusitis refers to inflammation of the sinus cavities, and is classified as acute sinusitis (short-term symptoms, anywhere from 1-12 weeks) and chronic sinusitis (longer-term symptoms, 12 weeks or more).
sinusitis.inflammation_text: While sinus inflammation is most often thought of as infectious (viral and bacterial), inflammation can also occur due to non-infectious processes, such as allergies, tobacco, or environmental irritants.
sinusitis.cold_text: The common cold is actually viral rhinosinusitis (nasal and sinus inflammation), which the body's own immune mechanisms typically resolve in 7-10 days.
sinusitis.diagnosis_viral_text: The vast majority (98%) of acute rhinosinusitis is viral. The only accurate indicator of the transition from viral rhinosinusitis to bacterial disease is symptom duration. As a rule of thumb, if rhinosinusitis symptoms are neither better nor worse after 10-14 days, bacterial infection is more likely and antibiotics are indicated.
sinusitis.diagnosis_evaluation_text: Dr. Lumbán will conduct a comprehensive evaluation, including a detailed medical history, ENT examination, and nasal endoscopy. This procedure is easily performed in the office with minimal discomfort and provides our physicians with a detailed assessment of nasal anatomy and inflammation status.
sinusitis.medical_treatment_text: When sinus inflammation is not resolved by the body's own mechanisms, or even with appropriate antibiotic therapy, then symptoms will persist and more intensive therapy may be indicated. This could include longer courses of antibiotics, concomitant use of decongestants and mucolytics, or possibly even anti-inflammatory steroids.
sinusitis.anatomical_text: Anatomical abnormalities may be detected, such as a deviated septum, nasal or sinus polyps, swelling, or abnormal secretions. These findings can help guide therapy and treatment response. CT imaging is used judiciously to fully evaluate the sinuses, providing information about the extent and distribution of sinus inflammation.
sinusitis.endoscopic_text: For patients whose inflammation is refractory and has little response to medical treatment, or who have significant nasal obstruction and/or anatomical abnormalities of the sinuses, surgery may be considered. Sinus surgery is performed endoscopically, prioritizing preservation of sinus function while restoring proper drainage, known as Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS).
sinusitis.endoscopic_note: It is most frequently performed under general anesthesia on an outpatient basis (i.e., same-day surgery). In some cases, CT imaging is used with image guidance technology, allowing real-time tracking of surgical instruments during the procedure.
sinusitis.risk_factors_text: If you suffer from frequent repeated sinus infections, or if you have truly chronic symptoms that do not respond to treatments, please make an appointment with Dr. Lumbán for a comprehensive evaluation. A complete history will be taken, an evaluation of nasal and sinus anatomy will be performed, and other factors that may need treatment will be identified, such as:
sinusitis.risk_tobacco_note: The harmful effects of tobacco use on nasal and sinus membranes cannot be overstated.
sinusitis.cta_chronic_text: Through endoscopic surgery, Dr. Lumbán can help you improve your health with minimal pain.

nasal-congestion.hero_subtitle: Specialized treatment for stuffy nose and breathing problems
nasal-congestion.title_h1: Nasal Congestion: Specialized Treatment for Stuffy Nose and Breathing Problems
nasal-congestion.intro_text: Nasal congestion occurs when the inside of the nose swells due to inflamed blood vessels.
nasal-congestion.intro_text2: The problem may also include rhinorrhea or runny nose. If excess mucus runs down the back of the throat (postnasal drip), it can cause coughing or sore throat.
nasal-congestion.warning_text: Untreated nasal congestion can lead to hearing problems, chronic fatigue, insomnia, headaches. It can also increase the frequency and volume of snoring, potentially leading to Sleep Apnea.
nasal-congestion.infections_text: The flu or acute sinusitis secondary to a common cold are caused by a viral infection. These viruses are airborne and cause inflammation of nasal tissues.

nasal-obstruction.intro_text: Nasal obstruction is a common symptom derived from various conditions that block, totally or partially, the airways. This condition manifests as if something restricts the airflow to breathe easily.
nasal-obstruction.causes_text: There are several factors that can compromise nasal function. Among the most common are:
nasal-obstruction.adenoids_text: They are glands located behind the nasal cavity. When inflamed, they narrow the respiratory passage, being the main cause of obstruction in children (although rare in adults).
nasal-obstruction.mucosa_text: Infections or allergies can inflame internal tissues. Conditions such as allergic rhinitis, vasomotor rhinitis, sinusitis, and nasal vestibulitis significantly restrict airflow.
nasal-obstruction.deviated_septum_text: The septum is the structure of bone and cartilage that divides the nose into two cavities. If crooked, it creates a fixed mechanical obstruction that does not respond to medication. In these cases, the only definitive solution is septoplasty.
nasal-obstruction.polyps_text: They are soft, non-cancerous growths in the lining of the nasal passages or sinuses that act as a physical barrier to air.
nasal-obstruction.turbinates_text: The inferior turbinates can excessively enlarge due to allergies or irritants. Although medical treatment helps, severe cases require surgical reduction.
nasal-obstruction.nasal_valve_text: The nasal valve is the narrowest area of the airway. If its walls are weak and collapse when inhaling, breathing becomes difficult.
nasal-obstruction.choanal_atresia_text: A congenital condition where babies are born with excess tissue blocking the nasal passages, requiring immediate attention.

Mientras que la inflamación del seno se: While sinus inflammation is most often thought of as infectious (viral and bacterial), inflammation can also occur due to non-infectious processes such as allergies, tobacco, or environmental irritants.
El resfriado común es en realidad una ri: The common cold is actually a viral rhinosinusitis (nasal and sinus inflammation), which the body's own immune mechanisms typically resolve in 7–10 days.
La gran mayoría (98%) de la enfermedad r: The vast majority (98%) of acute rhinosinusitis is viral. The only accurate indicator of transition from viral rhinosinusitis to bacterial disease is the duration of symptoms. As a general rule, if rhinosinusitis symptoms are neither better nor worse after 10–14 days, a bacterial infection is more likely and antibiotics are indicated.
El Dr. Lumbán llevará a cabo una evaluac: Dr. Lumbán will carry out a comprehensive evaluation, including a detailed medical history, ENT examination, and nasal endoscopy. This procedure is easily performed in the office with minimal discomfort and provides our physicians with a detailed assessment of nasal anatomy and the state of inflammation.
Cuando la inflamación sinusal no se borr: When sinus inflammation does not clear by the body's own mechanisms, or even with adequate antibiotic therapy, symptoms will persist and more intensive therapy may be indicated. This could include longer courses of antibiotics, concurrent use of decongestants and mucolytics, or possibly even anti-inflammatory steroids.
Pueden detectarse anomalías anatómicas,: Anatomical abnormalities can be detected, such as septal deviation, nasal or sinus polyps, swelling, or abnormal secretions. These findings can help guide therapy and response to treatment. CT imaging is used judiciously to fully evaluate the sinuses, providing information about the extent and distribution of inflammation in the nasal sinuses.
Para los pacientes cuya inflamación es r: For patients whose inflammation is refractory with poor response to medical treatment, or who have significant nasal obstruction and/or anatomical sinus abnormalities, surgery may be considered. Sinus surgery is performed endoscopically, prioritizing preservation of sinus function while restoring proper drainage, known as Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery (FESS).
Se realiza con más frecuencia bajo anest: It is most often performed under general anesthesia as an outpatient procedure (same-day surgery). In some cases, CT image-guidance technology is used, allowing real-time tracking of surgical instruments during the procedure.

To maintain our center of gravity, our central nervous system must receive these three signals and then correctly transmit them to the brain.
Cuando las señales de nuestros sentidos: When signals from our senses do not reach the cerebellum, or reach it with the wrong message, we experience this lack of communication as a loss of balance, dizziness.
Un trastorno del equilibrio a veces pued: A balance disorder can sometimes be a symptom of other medical conditions. Proper medical care, including a complete medical history and evaluation of the balance system, is important to identify the cause and provide appropriate treatment options.

Una cuestión clave con la pérdida de aud: A key issue with hearing loss is that it is generally gradual. While it can be sudden, hearing loss usually develops slowly over several years. The result is that most people with hearing loss are not aware of the magnitude of their problem.
